extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images of varied types and content.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.citeAs: Mathew, Minesh, Dimosthenis Karatzas, and C.V. Jawahar. "DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images." arXiv:2007.00398v3 [cs.CV], 5 Jan 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The authors downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset, prioritizing pages with tables, forms, lists and figures and trying to minimize binarized images. Questions and answers on the selected document images were collected with the help of remote workers using a web based annotation tool in three stages: question-answer collection, verification, and author review of mismatches.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from 6,071 industry documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning multiple industries and document types.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors hand picked pages from downloaded documents, tried to minimize binarized images because of poor image quality, and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text. The data was split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio into train, validation and test splits.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For analysis and experiments, OCR tokens were extracted using a commercial OCR application. For BERT question answering experiments, OCR tokens recognized on document images were serialized into a single string separated by spaces in top-left to bottom-right order, and answer spans were approximated by finding the first match of the answer string in the serialized OCR string.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it, with encouragement to add more than one ground truth answer when warranted. Workers were instructed to ask questions answerable using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. In stage 2, a worker was shown the image and questions from stage 1 but not the answers, and was required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag questions as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity, and such questions were excluded. In stage 3, if none of the answers from stage 1 matched exactly with any answers from stage 2, the question was sent for review where questions and answers were editable and the reviewer either accepted or ignored it. The third stage review was done by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The second stage verified first-stage annotations independently without showing prior answers. Questions could be flagged for invalidity, serious language issues, or ambiguity and were not included in the dataset. If answers from the first and second stages did not match exactly, the item was sent to a third-stage review by the authors, who could edit questions and answers or add new answers before accepting.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 question-answer pairs could be created per document image in stage 1; each question was answered again by one worker in stage 2, and mismatched cases were reviewed by the authors in stage 3.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers; a few volunteers from the authors' institution were used for measuring human performance.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and task aim to inspire a purpose-driven approach in document image analysis and recognition research, motivating simultaneous use of visual and textual cues for answering questions on document images and potentially driving methods that use low-level cues and high-level goals in solving problems of practical importance.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors prioritized non-binarized images and pages with tables, forms, lists and figures, and used many documents from food and nutrition related collections because they had a good number of non-binarized images. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the source library are binarized and binarization affects image quality. OCR is imperfect, and OCR errors can lead to wrong answers even when models ground questions correctly. Existing models show a large performance gap compared to human performance and need improvement especially on questions where understanding document structure is crucial. The paper also notes the need for models that better understand figures, text on photographs, and handwriting.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for Visual Question Answering on document images. It is split into train, validation, and test sets in an 80-10-10 ratio for model development and evaluation. The paper uses it to evaluate heuristic baselines, VQA models, reading comprehension models, and human performance.
